title: TS and Go collects answer different verdict words for an unpushed branch
body:
The dyo/94u seam — the TS collect (src/worker-verdict.ts, verdictFor) and the Go executor (internal/exec/cloudflaresandbox/collect.go, classify) — agree on the report-only refusal, but disagree on the verdict WORD for a branch that carries nothing at all (the push never landed): TS answers no-commits (its checks order no-commits first), Go answers missing-result (its checks the report first, by tick 19l's recorded order, which subprocess/collect.go documents as deliberate). Both fail the attempt, so no run misbehaves today — each attempt is collected by exactly one of the two — but these are two readers of one branch shape speaking different words of the closed verdict vocabulary, the drift class contracts/collect-vocabulary.json exists to catch. The property test test/property/worker-verdict.test.ts records the divergence, its minimal counterexample, and skips exactly that shape; a fix is either re-ordering verdictFor to the two-Go-consensus order, or recording the TS fact in the contract.
evidence: cloudflare/src/worker-verdict.ts verdictFor (no-commits checked first) vs internal/exec/cloudflaresandbox/collect.go classify (missing-result first); counterexample {branch_exists: true, commits: 0, result_exists: false, status: ""} → TS no-commits, Go missing-result
